extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of philosophy (readers interested in pragmatism and metaphysical method)
extracted.subtask_description: Using the pragmatic method to evaluate metaphysical claims about 'the One and the Many' by asking what practical differences various conceptions would make and by distinguishing concrete kinds of unity. Emphasis on moving from vague abstract doctrine to definite, experience-connected consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatic criterion — practical difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting the oneness to exist, what facts will be different in consequence? What will the unity be known-as? The pragmatic test asks: 'What is the practical value of the oneness for US?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat abstract notions pragmatically: pass from the vague to the definite by asking what concrete, experiential differences the theory would make. Use this question as the primary standard for assessing metaphysical claims; if a supposed unity has no practical consequences, its claim is of little pragmatic significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move from abstract to concrete (definiteness requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Asking such questions, we pass from the vague to the definite, from the abstract to the concrete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer conceptions that yield definite, ascertainable alterations in facts or behavior. Abstract labels (e.g. 'the universe') have little value unless you can specify how things would differ under that conception. Avoid staying at mere sublimity without traceable consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity as a subject of discourse (unity_of_discourse)
rubrics_metrics.description: The world is at least ONE SUBJECT OF DISCOURSE: we mean to cover the whole of it by our abstract term 'world' or 'universe', which expressly intends that no part shall be left out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that mere terminological or linguistic unity (being able to name the totality) is not a strong form of metaphysical unity — a 'chaos' named 'universe' has the same unity of discourse. Do not conflate the ability to speak of the whole with substantial unity that has practical consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity (spatial/temporal continuity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are they, for example, CONTINUOUS? Can you pass from one to another, keeping always in your one universe without any danger of falling out? Space and time are thus vehicles of continuity, by which the world's parts hang together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the practical importance of spatial and temporal continuity: these forms of union underpin our motor life and many practical capacities. A theory claiming unity should specify whether it entails such continuity and how that would affect practical operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lines of influence and systemic networks
rubrics_metrics.description: There are innumerable other paths of practical continuity among things. Lines of INFLUENCE (gravity, heat-conduction, electric, luminous, chemical) trace connection; human systems (colonial, postal, commercial, acquaintance-networks, love-systems) form definite networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat each kind of connexion or system as a separate grade/type of union. Note that systems have conductors and non-conductors: unity constituted by a given network can fail where non-conductors intervene. Evaluate theories by which networks they posit as real and how pervasive those networks are in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causal unity (unity of origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the minor causal influences among things should converge towards one common causal origin of them in the past, one great first cause for all that is, one might then speak of the absolute causal unity of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess metaphysical claims of a single causal origin (e.g., creation, Absolute cause) by their empirical and practical implications. James suggests leaving absolute causal unity unsettled unless strong evidence and practical difference warrant it; weigh alternatives (pluralistic eternal many) pragmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic unity (kinds and induction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important sort of union ... is their GENERIC UNITY. Things exist in kinds, there are many specimens in each kind, and what the 'kind' implies for one specimen, it implies also for every other specimen of that kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that generic unity is crucial for reasoning and induction: without kinds, logic from past to future would be impossible. Evaluate claims about universal genera by whether they secure the generalizations needed for practical prediction and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of purpose (teleological unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: UNITY OF PURPOSE. An enormous number of things in the world subserve a common purpose. ... an absolutely single, final and climacteric purpose subserved by all things without exception might conceivably be reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat teleological or final-purpose claims skeptically unless they yield plausible, testable consequences. Beware dogmatic assertions of absolute teleological unity (they tend to ignore conflicting, competing purposes and can be used to justify evils as instrumental). Pragmatism requires empirical evidence of purposive unification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic/narrative unity (things telling one story)
rubrics_metrics.description: AESTHETIC UNION among things also obtains ... Things tell a story. Their parts hang together so as to work out a climax. ... Whoever says that the whole world tells one story utters another of those monistic dogmas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between local narrative unities (episodic stories) and claims that the entire universe forms one dramatic whole. Evaluate claims of global narrative unity by whether events can be shown to fit into a single coherent story with practical consequence for understanding or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetic unity (one knower / epistemic unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: THE ONE KNOWER. The many exist only as objects for his thought -- exist in his dream, as it were; and AS HE KNOWS them, they have one purpose, form one system, tell one tale for him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess claims that there is an omniscient or absolute knower by asking what practical differences such an epistemic unity would make. Contrast an absolute, eternal knower with human-scale knowers; consider empirical plausibility and whether positing an Absolute adds testable content beyond psychological/mystical value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow degrees and avoid dogmatic absolutism
rubrics_metrics.description: Pragmatism ... must equally abjure absolute monism and absolute pluralism. The oneness and the manyness of it thus obtain in respects which can be separately named. ... Absolute unity brooks no degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor theories that permit degrees, gradations, and empirical determination of unity vs. disunity. Reject theories that require all-or-nothing commitments that cannot accommodate even minute independence or novelty; pragmatism prefers empirically decidable, gradable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical ascertainment over a priori dogma (anti-rigidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pluralism ... will allow you any amount, however great, of real union. How much of union there may be is a question that she thinks can only be decided empirically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precedence to empirical evidence and the progressive testing of claims rather than to a priori metaphysical dogmas. Use experience to tip the balance among hypotheses about unity and multiplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservative theory-change — knowledge grows in spots
rubrics_metrics.description: Our knowledge grows IN SPOTS. ... We keep unaltered as much of our old knowledge, as many of our old prejudices and beliefs, as we can. We patch and tinker more than we renew. The novelty soaks in; it stains the ancient mass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or proposing theoretical revisions, expect gradual, piecemeal change that preserves much of the antecedent framework (common-sense 'ground-plan'). New theories should account for and incorporate entrenched beliefs/categories unless decisive practical reasons exist to overturn them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for common-sense categories (denkmittel)
rubrics_metrics.description: OUR FUNDAMENTAL WAYS OF THINKING ABOUT THINGS ARE DISCOVERIES OF EXCEEDINGLY REMOTE ANCESTORS ... They form one great stage of equilibrium in the human mind's development, the stage of common sense. In philosophy it means ... use of certain intellectual forms or categories of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for the persistence and pragmatic utility of common-sense intellectual forms when judging theories. New conceptual schemes must show they improve on entrenched denkmittel in ways that produce concrete gains in handling experience (cf. Descartes vs Euclid example).
